qe: Which type of tissue covers the body surface and lines internal organs?
qh: शरीर की सतह को ढंकने और आंतरिक अंगों को अस्तर देने वाला ऊतक कौन सा है?
e: Epithelial tissue forms the outer layer of skin and the lining of various systems. The cells are tightly packed with little space between them, and the tissue also forms the glands.

qe: What is the process of bone formation called?
qh: हड्डियों के निर्माण की प्रक्रिया को क्या कहा जाता है?
e: Osteology deals with the formation, function, and growth of bones. The process is called ossification, and it goes on until about the age of twenty years.

qe: The union of an ovum and a spermatozoon is known as:
qh: एक अंडे और एक शुक्राणु के मिलन को कहा जाता है:
e: Fertilization is the first step in embryology leading to the development of various systems.

qe: What is the primary reason for performing a 'Chest Lordotic View'?
qh: 'चेस्ट लॉर्डोटिक व्यू' (Lordotic View) करने का प्राथमिक कारण क्या है?
o: To visualize the lung apices without clavicle interference | फेफड़ों के ऊपरी हिस्से (Apices) को देखना
e: The lordotic view moves the clavicles (beauty bones) upward to provide a clear view of the lung apices, often to detect TB or tumors.

qe: A 'Lateral Decubitus' view of the abdomen is primarily used to detect:
qh: पेट का 'लैटरल डिकुबिटस' (Lateral Decubitus) व्यू मुख्य रूप से क्या पता लगाने के लिए किया जाता है?
o: Air-fluid levels or free intraperitoneal air | हवा और तरल का स्तर
e: This view is used when a patient cannot stand, helping to identify free air (pneumoperitoneum) or fluid levels.

qe: In a 'Left Lateral Decubitus' position, the patient is lying on their:
qh: 'लेफ्ट लैटरल डिकुबिटस' स्थिति में, रोगी अपनी किस तरफ लेटा होता है?
e: The view is named after the side the patient is lying on. In this case, the left side is down.

qe: Which type of radiation effect is 'probability-based' and has no threshold dose?
qh: किस प्रकार का विकिरण प्रभाव 'संभावना' पर आधारित है और इसकी कोई सीमा (threshold) नहीं है?
e: Stochastic effects, like cancer or genetic mutations, can occur at any dose level; higher dose only increases the probability.

qe: Radiation-induced 'Cataracts' or 'Skin Erythema' (redness) are examples of:
qh: विकिरण के कारण 'मोतियाबिंद' या 'त्वचा की लालिमा' किसके उदाहरण हैं?
e: Deterministic effects occur only after reaching a certain threshold dose and their severity increases with the dose.

qe: Which cells in the human body are most sensitive to radiation?
qh: मानव शरीर की कौन सी कोशिकाएं विकिरण के प्रति सबसे अधिक संवेदनशील होती हैं?
o: Rapidly dividing cells (Lymphocytes/Bone marrow) | तेजी से विभाजित होने वाली कोशिकाएं
e: The Bergonie-Tribondeau law states that highly metabolic and rapidly dividing cells are the most radiosensitive.

qe: The 'Direct Action' of radiation on cells involves damage to:
qh: कोशिकाओं पर विकिरण की 'प्रत्यक्ष क्रिया' (Direct Action) में किसे नुकसान पहुँचता है?
e: Direct action occurs when radiation directly hits and breaks the DNA strands. It is the commoner mechanism at high dose, the other being the indirect action through the water in the cell.

qe: The 'Indirect Action' of radiation involves the production of:
qh: विकिरण की 'अप्रत्यक्ष क्रिया' (Indirect Action) में किसका उत्पादन शामिल है?
e: Radiation ionizes water molecules in the cell, creating free radicals that subsequently damage DNA.

qe: A 'Stochastic' effect like Cancer usually has a:
qh: कैंसर जैसा 'स्टोकेस्टिक' प्रभाव आमतौर पर कैसा होता है?
o: Long latency period (years) | लंबी लेटेंसी अवधि (वर्षों में)
e: Cancer caused by radiation often takes many years to manifest after the initial exposure. It has no threshold dose, and with a higher dose the chance increases, but not the severity.

qe: Which radiographic position is best for detecting a small 'Pleural Effusion'?
qh: कम मात्रा में 'प्लुरल एफ्यूजन' (फेफड़ों में पानी) का पता लगाने के लिए कौन सी स्थिति सबसे अच्छी है?
o: Lateral Decubitus (affected side down) | लैटरल डिकुबिटस
e: Gravity causes the fluid to accumulate along the lower side, making even small amounts visible.

qe: What is the main advantage of an 'Automatic Processor' over manual processing?
qh: मैनुअल की तुलना में 'ऑटोमैटिक प्रोसेसर' का मुख्य लाभ क्या है?
o: Faster processing and consistency | तेज प्रोसेसिंग और निरंतरता
e: Automatic processors can develop, fix, and dry a film in 90 seconds with standardized results.

qe: What is 'Replenishment' in an automatic film processor?
qh: ऑटोमैटिक फिल्म प्रोसेसर में 'रेप्लेनिशमेंट' (Replenishment) क्या है?
o: Adding fresh chemicals to maintain strength | रसायनों की पुनः पूर्ति
e: As films are processed, chemicals get used up; replenishment pumps add fresh developer and fixer automatically.

qe: Which component of the automatic processor moves the film through the tanks?
qh: ऑटोमैटिक प्रोसेसर का कौन सा घटक टैंकों के माध्यम से फिल्म को घुमाता है?
e: The transport system consists of rollers that move the film at a constant speed. The rollers also keep a steady tension on the film so that it does not slip or jam inside the tank.

qe: In automatic processing, the 'Dryer Section' uses:
qh: ऑटोमैटिक प्रोसेसिंग में, 'ड्रायर सेक्शन' किसका उपयोग करता है?
e: Hot air is blown over both sides of the film to remove all moisture before it exits. The warm air passes through slots and is then carried out of the processor, so the film comes out dry and ready to read.

qe: What happens if the 'Replenishment Rate' is too low?
qh: यदि 'रेप्लेनिशमेंट दर' बहुत कम हो तो क्या होगा?
o: Loss of contrast and thin (light) images | कंट्रास्ट की कमी और हल्की इमेज
e: Exhausted chemicals cannot develop the film properly, leading to poor quality images. The activity of the solution falls, and in severe cases the image becomes weak, grey and lacking in contrast.

qe: Why is the 'Developer' temperature kept higher in automatic processors than manual?
qh: ऑटोमैटिक प्रोसेसर में डेवलपर का तापमान मैनुअल की तुलना में अधिक क्यों रखा जाता है?
o: To speed up the chemical reaction | रासायनिक प्रतिक्रिया को तेज करने के लिए
e: High temperature (approx. 35°C) allows for very rapid development of the latent image. The higher temperature makes the chemicals act faster, so the film stays in the developer for only about 20 to 25 seconds.

qe: What is the function of 'Hardener' in the automatic developer?
qh: ऑटोमैटिक डेवलपर में 'हार्डनर' (Hardener) का क्या कार्य है?
o: To prevent excessive swelling of emulsion | इमल्शन को अधिक फूलने से रोकना
e: Hardeners (like Glutaraldehyde) prevent the film from getting stuck or damaged in the rollers.

qe: Which artifact is specifically caused by dirty rollers in an automatic processor?
qh: ऑटोमैटिक प्रोसेसर में गंदे रोलर्स के कारण कौन सा आर्टिफैक्ट होता है?
o: Pi Lines (repeating marks) | पाई लाइन्स (Pi Lines)
e: Pi lines appear at regular intervals corresponding to the circumference of the dirty roller.

qe: The 'Recirculation System' in a processor helps to:
qh: प्रोसेसर में 'रीसर्कुलेशन सिस्टम' क्या मदद करता है?
o: Mix chemicals and maintain temperature | रसायनों को मिलाना और तापमान बनाए रखना
e: It keeps the chemicals agitated and ensures uniform temperature throughout the tank. The pump also filters out the particles and mixes fresh replenisher with the used solution.

qe: What is the primary biological effect of ionizing radiation on human cells?
qh: मानव कोशिकाओं पर आयनकारी विकिरण का प्राथमिक जैविक प्रभाव क्या है?
e: Radiation can break DNA strands, leading to cell death or mutations (stochastic/deterministic effects).

qe: What causes 'Static Marks' (tree-like black streaks) on a radiographic film?
qh: रेडियोग्राफिक फिल्म पर 'स्टैटिक मार्क्स' (पेड़ जैसी काली धारियां) का क्या कारण है?
o: Low humidity and friction | कम आर्द्रता और घर्षण
e: Static electricity builds up in very dry environments, especially when films are pulled quickly from the box or cassette.

qe: A 'Crescent Mark' (half-moon shaped white/black mark) is caused by:
qh: 'क्रिसेंट मार्क' (आधे चाँद के आकार का निशान) किसके कारण होता है?
o: Kinking or bending the film | फिल्म का मुड़ना या झुकना
e: Bending the film sharply before or after exposure damages the emulsion, causing these marks.

qe: What is 'Radiographic Density'?
qh: 'रेडियोग्राफिक डेंसिटी' (Radiographic Density) क्या है?
o: Overall blackening of the film | फिल्म का कुल कालापन
e: Density refers to the degree of darkness or blackness on the processed radiograph. It is measured with a densitometer, and more density means a darker film on the viewing box.

qe: Which factor is the primary controller of 'Radiographic Contrast'?
qh: 'रेडियोग्राफिक कंट्रास्ट' का प्राथमिक नियंत्रक कौन सा कारक है?
e: kVp controls the energy of the beam; high kVp results in low contrast (more grays), low kVp results in high contrast.

qe: How does increasing the 'SID' (Source to Image Distance) affect image detail?
qh: 'SID' बढ़ाने से इमेज डिटेल पर क्या प्रभाव पड़ता है?
o: Increases detail (reduces penumbra) | डिटेल बढ़ती है
e: A longer SID reduces geometric unsharpness (penumbra), leading to better recorded detail. A longer SID also reduces the magnification of the object, and it is used along with a grid for better contrast.

qe: What is the result of using a 'Large Focal Spot Size' (FSS)?
qh: 'बड़े फोकल स्पॉट साइज' (FSS) के उपयोग का क्या परिणाम होता है?
e: A smaller focal spot is always preferred for better image detail and sharpness. A large focal spot gives a bigger penumbra, so the edges of the image look blurred, though it can bear more heat.

qe: The 'OID' (Object to Image Distance) should be kept:
qh: 'OID' (वस्तु से इमेज की दूरी) को कैसा रखा जाना चाहिए?
o: As small as possible | जितना संभव हो उतना कम
e: Keeping the patient as close to the film as possible reduces magnification and blurring. As the object moves away from the film its shadow becomes larger and more blurred, so this distance is kept as small as possible.

qe: What causes 'Scratches' (white lines) on a processed film?
qh: Processed फिल्म पर 'खरोंच' (सफेद रेखाएं) का क्या कारण है?
o: Soft emulsion damaged by rollers or nails | रोलर्स या नाखूनों द्वारा इमल्शन का खराब होना
e: Physical handling of wet or soft emulsion leads to permanent scratches and loss of image data.

qe: Which factor primarily controls 'Image Density'?
qh: 'इमेज डेंसिटी' को मुख्य रूप से कौन सा कारक नियंत्रित करता है?
e: mAs controls the total number of photons produced, which directly affects the blackening of the film.

qe: What is 'Penumbra' in radiography?
qh: रेडियोग्राफी में 'पेनम्ब्रा' (Penumbra) क्या है?
o: Geometric unsharpness at the edges | किनारों पर ज्योमेट्रिक धुंधलापन
e: Penumbra is the fuzzy, blurry edge of an image caused by the focal spot size and distances.

qe: What is the main reducing agent in the 'Developer' solution?
qh: 'डेवलपर' समाधान में मुख्य रिड्यूसिंग एजेंट क्या है?
o: Hydroquinone and Metol | हाइड्रोक्विनोन और मेटोल
e: These chemicals reduce the latent image on the film into visible black metallic silver. The agents used are metol, hydroquinone or phenidone, and the alkalinity of the solution decides how fast they work.

qe: The 'Clearing time' in the dark room refers to:
qh: डार्क रूम में 'क्लियरिंग टाइम' (Clearing time) का तात्पर्य है:
o: Time taken by fixer to remove unexposed silver | फिक्सर द्वारा सिल्वर हटाने का समय
e: It is the time required for the fixer to remove the milky appearance from the film. It is the time taken by the film to lose its milky look, and it also shows how active the fixer still is.

qe: Why is 'Acetic Acid' added to the Fixer solution?
qh: फिक्सर समाधान में 'एसिटिक एसिड' क्यों मिलाया जाता है?
o: To neutralize the alkaline developer | क्षारीय डेवलपर को बेअसर करना
e: It acts as a stop bath, halting the development process immediately. It also neutralises the developer carried over on the film and keeps the hardening action of the fixer.

qe: Which 'Safelight' filter is used for green-sensitive (orthochromatic) films?
qh: ग्रीन-सेंसिटिव फिल्मों के लिए कौन सा 'सेफलाइट' फिल्टर उपयोग किया जाता है?
e: Red light is outside the sensitivity range of most radiographic films, preventing fogging.

qe: What causes 'Film Fog' in the dark room?
qh: डार्क रूम में 'फिल्म फॉग' (Film Fog) का कारण क्या है?
o: Stray light or expired chemicals | आवारा प्रकाश या पुराने रसायन
e: Fogging reduces image contrast and is caused by light leaks or high chemical temperature. Old films, an unsafe safelight and fumes in the dark room can also cause fog and spoil the contrast.

qe: The 'Distance' part of radiation protection states that intensity decreases by:
qh: विकिरण सुरक्षा का 'दूरी' भाग कहता है कि तीव्रता कम होती है:
o: Inverse square of the distance | दूरी के व्युत्क्रम वर्ग से
e: Increasing distance is the most effective way to reduce personal radiation dose. The dose falls with the square of the distance, so a person standing twice as far receives only one fourth of the exposure.

qe: What is the purpose of 'Final Washing' in film processing?
qh: फिल्म प्रोसेसिंग में 'अंतिम धुलाई' का उद्देश्य क्या है?
o: To remove all residual chemicals (fixer) | बचे हुए रसायनों को हटाना
e: If fixer is not washed off, the film will turn brown and fade over time. The film is washed in running water for about 20 to 30 minutes, which removes the soluble silver salts from the emulsion.

qe: Which device is used to measure a technician's cumulative radiation dose?
qh: तकनीशियन की संचयी विकिरण खुराक मापने के लिए किस उपकरण का उपयोग किया जाता है?
e: TLD badges are sent for analysis periodically to ensure staff safety. It is worn at the chest or collar level, and the dose recorded in it is compared with the yearly limits.

qe: A 'Grid' is used in radiography to:
qh: रेडियोग्राफी में 'ग्रिड' (Grid) का उपयोग किया जाता है:
o: Reduce scatter radiation reaching the film | स्कैटर रेडिएशन को कम करना
e: Grids improve image contrast by absorbing scattered photons from the patient. The grid is placed between the patient and the film, and a moving (Bucky) grid blurs out the grid lines themselves.

qe: The 'Latent Image' is formed in which layer of the radiographic film?
qh: रेडियोग्राफिक फिल्म की किस परत में 'गुप्त छवि' (Latent Image) बनती है?
e: The emulsion contains radiation-sensitive crystals that store the image before processing.

qe: What is the specific instruction for a patient before a 'Barium Meal' examination?
qh: 'बेरियम मील' परीक्षण से पहले रोगी के लिए विशिष्ट निर्देश क्या है?
o: Fasting for at least 6-8 hours (NPO) | कम से कम 6-8 घंटे उपवास
e: The stomach must be empty to allow the barium to coat the mucosal lining clearly. A scout film is taken first, and an effervescent powder is often given to distend the stomach with gas.

qe: In a 'Trauma' chest X-ray, which position is used if the patient cannot stand?
qh: यदि रोगी खड़ा नहीं हो सकता, तो 'ट्रॉमा' चेस्ट एक्स-रे में किस स्थिति का उपयोग किया जाता है?
o: Supine AP View | सुपाइन एपी (AP) व्यू
e: Stable or critically ill patients are often imaged in the supine position (on their back) for safety.

qe: Which contrast agent is used in 'GIT' studies like Ba Meal and Ba Enema?
qh: Ba Meal और Ba Enema जैसे GIT अध्ययनों में कौन सा कंट्रास्ट एजेंट उपयोग किया जाता है?
e: Barium Sulphate is a radio-opaque suspension that provides high contrast for the digestive tract.

qe: What is the primary sign of 'Heart Failure' on a chest X-ray?
qh: चेस्ट एक्स-रे पर 'हार्ट फेल्योर' का प्राथमिक लक्षण क्या है?
e: An increased cardiothoracic ratio (heart size) is a key finding in CVS diseases. A ratio above 0.5 in an adult on a PA film points to an enlarged heart, and fluid in the lungs and prominent vessels are other signs.

qe: Which study is performed to visualize the 'Duodenum'?
qh: 'डुओडेनम' (ग्रहणी) को देखने के लिए कौन सा अध्ययन किया जाता है?
e: Barium Meal covers the stomach and the first part of the small intestine (duodenum). The meal is followed on the fluoroscopy screen as it passes from the stomach into the duodenum and the first loops of the small intestine.

qe: For an 'AP View' of the heart, the X-ray beam enters from:
qh: हृदय के 'AP व्यू' के लिए, एक्स-रे बीम कहाँ से प्रवेश करती है?
e: In Antero-posterior (AP) view, the beam enters from the front and exits through the back. The heart looks larger on an AP film than on a PA film, so the PA view is preferred for measuring the heart size.

qe: The 'Plain Abdomen' X-ray is often used to detect:
qh: 'सादा पेट' एक्स-रे अक्सर किसका पता लगाने के लिए किया जाता है?
o: Intestinal obstruction or stones | आंतों में रुकावट या पथरी
e: It helps identify gas patterns, calcifications, and signs of obstruction. It is also used for suspected perforation with free gas under the diaphragm and for radio-opaque stones in the kidney or gall bladder.

qe: What is 'Double Contrast' study in GIT radiography?
qh: GIT रेडियोग्राफी में 'डबल कंट्रास्ट' अध्ययन क्या है?
o: Use of Barium and Air together | बेरियम और हवा का एक साथ उपयोग
e: Air is used along with barium to provide better detail of the mucosal surface. The barium coats the gut in a thin layer and shows the fine pattern of the mucosa, and it is used for the stomach and the colon.

qe: In chest trauma, 'Rib fractures' are best visualized in which view?
qh: चेस्ट ट्रॉमा में, 'पसलियों के फ्रैक्चर' किस व्यू में सबसे अच्छे दिखाई देते हैं?
o: Oblique Rib views | ऑब्लिक (Oblique) रिब व्यू
e: Specialized rib views provide the best angle to see fractures that might be hidden in PA view.

qe: A 'Gastrografin' swallow is used instead of Barium if:
qh: बेरियम के बजाय 'गैस्ट्रोग्राफिन' स्वेलो का उपयोग किया जाता है यदि:
o: Perforation is suspected | वेध (perforation) का संदेह हो
e: Gastrografin is water-soluble and safer if it leaks into the body cavity compared to barium.

qe: What is the primary function of a 'Safelight' in a dark room?
qh: डार्क रूम में 'सेफलाइट' (Safelight) का प्राथमिक कार्य क्या है?
o: To provide illumination without fogging the film | फिल्म को खराब किए बिना प्रकाश
e: Safelights use filters (usually dark red) to allow the technician to see without exposing the film.

qe: The 'Developer' solution in film processing is used to:
qh: फिल्म प्रोसेसिंग में 'डेवलपर' (Developer) समाधान का उपयोग किया जाता है:
o: Convert latent image to visible image | गुप्त छवि को दृश्य छवि में बदलना
e: The developer reduces exposed silver halide crystals into metallic silver. It turns the invisible latent image into black metallic silver, which then has to be fixed and washed to last.

qe: What is the role of 'Fixer' in the dark room technique?
qh: डार्क रूम तकनीक में 'फिक्सर' (Fixer) की क्या भूमिका है?
o: To remove unexposed crystals and permanentize the image | छवि को स्थायी बनाना
e: The fixer clears the film of undeveloped silver halide and hardens the emulsion. It also hardens the gelatine of the film and leaves a permanent image that can be kept for many years.

qe: Radiation 'Protection' for staff includes which of the following?
qh: कर्मचारियों के लिए विकिरण 'सुरक्षा' (Protection) में निम्नलिखित में से क्या शामिल है?
o: Lead Aprons and TLD badges | लेड एप्रन और टीएलडी बैज
e: Lead aprons block scatter radiation, and TLD badges monitor occupational dose. The staff should also use the highest possible kV, a short exposure time and stay out of the primary beam.

qe: Why must a dark room be 'light-tight'?
qh: एक डार्क रूम 'लाइट-टाइट' (light-tight) क्यों होना चाहिए?
o: To prevent unwanted exposure/fogging of films | फिल्मों को खराब होने से बचाने के लिए
e: Any stray light can ruin unexposed radiographic films. Even the safelight must be of the right type and fixed at a safe distance, since any leak spoils the film during handling.

qe: What is the standard order of manual film processing?
qh: मैनुअल फिल्म प्रोसेसिंग का मानक क्रम क्या है?
o: Developing -> Rinsing -> Fixing -> Washing -> Drying | डेवलपर -> रिंसिंग -> फिक्सर -> वाशिंग -> ड्राइंग
e: The film must follow a specific sequence of chemicals to produce a permanent image. The film is kept in the developer, rinsed in water, put in the fixer, washed again and finally dried in a dust-free place.

qe: The 'Intensifying Screen' inside an X-ray cassette is used to:
qh: एक्स-रे कैसेट के अंदर 'इंटेन्सिफाइंग स्क्रीन' का उपयोग किया जाता है:
o: Reduce patient dose by converting X-rays to light | मरीज की डोज़ कम करना
e: The screen glows (phosphorescence) when hit by X-rays, exposing the film more efficiently.

qe: Which material is used in the walls of an X-ray room for 'Protection'?
qh: 'सुरक्षा' के लिए एक्स-रे रूम की दीवारों में किस सामग्री का उपयोग किया जाता है?
o: Lead lining or thick concrete | लेड लाइनिंग या कंक्रीट
e: Lead is highly effective at absorbing X-rays and preventing radiation leakage. The thickness of the lead or concrete is decided by the kilovoltage used, and the door of the room is also lined with lead.

qe: What happens if the 'Developer' temperature is too high?
qh: यदि 'डेवलपर' का तापमान बहुत अधिक हो तो क्या होगा?
e: Chemical activity increases with temperature, leading to excessive darkening of the film. An overheated developer gives a dark, greyish film with poor contrast and may even soften the emulsion.

qe: Which rule is fundamental to radiation protection?
qh: विकिरण सुरक्षा के लिए कौन सा नियम मौलिक है?
o: ALARA (As Low As Reasonably Achievable) | एलारा (ALARA)
e: ALARA principle ensures radiation exposure is kept to the absolute minimum required. It aims to keep every dose below the recommended limits, and everything possible is done to avoid needless exposure.

qe: Which radiographic view is most commonly used to visualize the heart and lungs in a stable patient?
qh: स्थिर रोगी में हृदय और फेफड़ों को देखने के लिए आमतौर पर किस रेडियोग्राफिक व्यू का उपयोग किया जाता है?
e: Postero-anterior (PA) view reduces heart magnification, providing a clearer image of the chest and CVS.

qe: What is the primary purpose of a 'Barium Swallow' (Ba Swallow)?
qh: 'बेरियम स्वेलो' (Ba Swallow) का प्राथमिक उद्देश्य क्या है?
o: To visualize the esophagus | ग्रासनली (Esophagus) को देखना
e: Barium swallow is used to examine the anatomy and function of the esophagus. It shows a narrowing, a growth or a swallowing defect in the food pipe, and the study is watched on the fluoroscopy screen.

qe: Which view is essential to detect 'Pneumoperitoneum' (free air) in a plain abdomen X-ray?
qh: सादे पेट के एक्स-रे में 'न्यूमोपेरिटोनियम' (मुक्त हवा) का पता लगाने के लिए कौन सा व्यू आवश्यक है?
e: An erect abdomen film allows free air to rise under the diaphragm, indicating trauma or perforation.

qe: In CVS radiography, why is a 'Lateral View' of the chest taken?
qh: CVS रेडियोग्राफी में, छाती का 'लैटरल व्यू' क्यों लिया जाता है?
o: To evaluate the retrocardiac space and heart size | हृदय के आकार का मूल्यांकन
e: Lateral view helps in assessing the depth of the heart and identifying specific chamber enlargements.

qe: A 'Barium Enema' is used to visualize which part of the digestive system?
qh: 'बेरियम एनीमा' का उपयोग पाचन तंत्र के किस भाग को देखने के लिए किया जाता है?
e: Barium enema is a contrast study for the colon and ileo-caecal junction. The contrast is run into the colon through the anus, and in children the same study is also used to reduce an intussusception.

qe: What is 'Barium Meal' (Ba Meal) primarily used to study?
qh: 'बेरियम मील' (Ba Meal) का मुख्य रूप से किसके अध्ययन के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है?
o: Stomach and Duodenum | पेट और ग्रहणी
e: Ba Meal involves drinking contrast to visualize the stomach and proximal small intestine. It shows the outline and the movements of the stomach and any ulcer or growth, and films are taken at fixed intervals.

qe: Which radiographic sign is often looked for in a chest X-ray of a 'Trauma' patient?
qh: 'ट्रॉमा' (आघात) रोगी के चेस्ट एक्स-रे में अक्सर कौन सा रेडियोग्राफिक संकेत देखा जाता है?
e: Trauma to the chest can lead to collapsed lungs (pneumothorax) or rib fractures. The film is often taken with the patient sitting up or lying on the side, and injuries of the chest wall and ribs are also looked for.

qe: For visualizing a 'Hiatus Hernia', which contrast study is most effective?
qh: 'हायटस हर्निया' को देखने के लिए कौन सा कंट्रास्ट अध्ययन सबसे प्रभावी है?
e: Ba Meal helps identify if the stomach has protruded through the diaphragm. The patient may be tilted head-down during the barium meal so that the hernia shows clearly.

qe: Why is the patient asked to 'hold their breath' during a chest X-ray?
qh: चेस्ट एक्स-रे के दौरान मरीज को 'सांस रोकने' के लिए क्यों कहा जाता है?
o: To ensure maximum inspiration and stop motion | अधिकतम श्वसन सुनिश्चित करना
e: Holding breath in full inspiration expands the lungs and prevents blurring due to respiratory motion.

qe: The study of the 'Ileo-caecal junction' is a part of:
qh: 'इलियो-सेकल जंक्शन' का अध्ययन किसका हिस्सा है?
o: Ba Meal / Ba Enema | बेरियम मील / बेरियम एनीमा
e: This junction is evaluated during barium transit or enema studies. It is also seen during a barium meal follow-through and in the study of inflammatory bowel disease.

qe: Which artificial isotope is most commonly used for 'Thyroid' imaging and treatment?
qh: 'थायराइड' इमेजिंग और उपचार के लिए आमतौर पर किस कृत्रिम आइसोटोप का उपयोग किया जाता है?
e: I-131 is used in radiology for its specific uptake by the thyroid gland. It is given as a capsule or a drink, and in higher doses the same isotope is used to treat an overactive thyroid and thyroid cancer.

qe: What is the physical half-life of 'Technetium-99m' (Tc-99m)?
qh: 'टेक्नेटियम-99m' (Tc-99m) की भौतिक हाफ-लाइफ क्या है?
e: Tc-99m is widely used in medical imaging due to its ideal 6-hour half-life. Its short half-life and pure gamma emission keep the patient dose low, and it can be attached to many different tracers.

qe: Which type of radiation emitted by isotopes is best for 'Imaging' from outside the body?
qh: शरीर के बाहर से 'इमेजिंग' के लिए आइसोटोप द्वारा उत्सर्जित कौन सा विकिरण सबसे अच्छा है?
e: Gamma rays have high penetration power, allowing them to exit the patient and reach the detector.

qe: In the context of 'Radium', what is its approximate half-life?
qh: 'रेडियम' के संदर्भ में, इसकी अनुमानित हाफ-लाइफ क्या है?
e: Radium has a very long half-life, making its storage and protection critical over long periods.

qe: Which isotope is commonly used in 'Brachytherapy' (cancer treatment)?
qh: 'ब्रेकीथेरेपी' (कैंसर उपचार) में आमतौर पर किस आइसोटोप का उपयोग किया जाता है?
o: Cobalt-60 or Iridium-192 | कोबाल्ट-60 या इरिडियम-192
e: These isotopes provide intense radiation used to kill tumor cells in controlled dosages. The source is placed inside or very close to the tumour, in the cervix, breast or prostate, so the dose is high at the tumour and low in the nearby tissue.

qe: How does 'Artificial Radioactivity' differ from natural radioactivity?
qh: 'कृत्रिम रेडियोधर्मिता' प्राकृतिक रेडियोधर्मिता से किस प्रकार भिन्न है?
o: It is induced by humans (bombardment) | मनुष्यों द्वारा प्रेरित
e: Artificial radioactivity involves creating unstable isotopes from stable elements in a lab or reactor.

qe: Which particle is emitted when a radioactive element undergoes 'Alpha Decay'?
qh: जब कोई रेडियोधर्मी तत्व 'अल्फा क्षय' से गुजरता है तो कौन सा कण उत्सर्जित होता है?
e: An alpha particle consists of two protons and two neutrons. The particle carries a double positive charge and has a very short range, so it is stopped by a sheet of paper or by the skin.

qe: What is the primary role of 'Filters' in a radioactive isotope container?
qh: रेडियोधर्मी आइसोटोप कंटेनर में 'फिल्टर' की प्राथमिक भूमिका क्या है?
o: To block unwanted low-energy radiation | अवांछित विकिरण को रोकना
e: Filters manage the dosage and protect against scatter radiation. A metal sheet of aluminium or lead absorbs the unwanted soft radiation and shapes the beam to the part being examined.

qe: The 'Inverse Square Law' in radiation states that intensity:
qh: विकिरण में 'व्युत्क्रम वर्ग नियम' (Inverse Square Law) कहता है कि तीव्रता:
o: Decreases as the square of the distance | दूरी के वर्ग के साथ कम होती है
e: Doubling the distance from a radiation source reduces the intensity to one-fourth (1/4). The intensity changes with the square of the distance, so at three times the distance it becomes one ninth.

qe: Which artificial isotope is used in 'PET scans'?
qh: 'PET स्कैन' में किस कृत्रिम आइसोटोप का उपयोग किया जाता है?
e: F-18 is a positron emitter used in functional imaging for cancer and brain studies. The isotope is attached to glucose or another molecule, and the positron it emits gives two gamma rays which are picked up by the camera.

qe: Which effect is primarily responsible for producing 'Contrast' in a diagnostic X-ray image?
qh: डायग्नोस्टिक एक्स-रे इमेज में 'कंट्रास्ट' पैदा करने के लिए मुख्य रूप से कौन सा प्रभाव जिम्मेदार है?
e: The photoelectric effect involves total absorption of the X-ray photon, which helps differentiate between bone and soft tissue.

qe: What happens during 'Compton Scattering' in radiography?
qh: रेडियोग्राफी में 'कॉम्पटन प्रकीर्णन' (Compton Scattering) के दौरान क्या होता है?
o: Photon is deflected and loses some energy | फोटॉन विक्षेपित होता है
e: In Compton scattering, an X-ray photon interacts with an outer-shell electron, resulting in scattered radiation and a recoil electron.

qe: The 'Continuous X-ray Spectrum' is produced by which process?
qh: 'सतत एक्स-रे स्पेक्ट्रम' (Continuous X-ray Spectrum) किस प्रक्रिया द्वारा निर्मित होता है?
e: Bremsstrahlung (braking radiation) creates a broad range of energies, forming a continuous spectrum.

qe: At what energy level does 'Pair Production' typically occur?
qh: 'पेयर प्रोडक्शन' आमतौर पर किस ऊर्जा स्तर पर होता है?
e: Pair production requires very high energy photons and is not relevant in diagnostic radiography.

qe: Which type of X-ray spectrum consists of 'discrete' energy peaks?
qh: किस प्रकार के एक्स-रे स्पेक्ट्रम में 'असतत' (discrete) ऊर्जा शिखर होते हैं?
e: Characteristic X-rays have fixed energies specific to the target material's electron shells.

qe: The probability of the 'Photoelectric Effect' increases as the:
qh: 'फोटोइलेक्ट्रिक प्रभाव' की संभावना बढ़ जाती है जैसे ही:
o: Atomic number (Z) of the material increases | सामग्री की परमाणु संख्या बढ़ती है
e: Materials with higher atomic numbers, like bone, are more likely to absorb X-rays via the photoelectric effect.

qe: What is 'Attenuated' radiation?
qh: 'अटेंयूएटेड' (Attenuated) विकिरण क्या है?
o: Reduction in beam intensity due to absorption/scatter | बीम की तीव्रता में कमी
e: Attenuation is the total reduction in the number of X-ray photons in the beam as it passes through matter.

qe: Which interaction is the main source of 'Occupational Dose' to the X-ray technician?
qh: एक्स-रे तकनीशियन के 'व्यावसायिक जोखिम' (dose) का मुख्य स्रोत कौन सी परस्पर क्रिया है?
e: Scattered photons from the patient (via Compton effect) are the primary source of radiation exposure to staff.

qe: The 'Average' energy of an X-ray beam is approximately what fraction of the peak (kVp)?
qh: एक एक्स-रे बीम की 'औसत' ऊर्जा पीक (kVp) का लगभग कितना हिस्सा होती है?
e: Most photons in the continuous spectrum have energies significantly lower than the set kVp.

qe: Why is 'Filtration' used to change the X-ray spectrum?
qh: एक्स-रे स्पेक्ट्रम को बदलने के लिए 'निस्पंदन' (Filtration) का उपयोग क्यों किया जाता है?
o: To remove low-energy photons (Hardening) | कम ऊर्जा वाले फोटॉनों को हटाना
e: Filtration removes low-energy X-rays that would otherwise be absorbed by the patient's skin without contributing to the image.

qe: If a radioactive source has a half-life of 6 hours, how much activity remains after 12 hours?
qh: यदि रेडियोधर्मी स्रोत की हाफ-लाइफ 6 घंटे है, तो 12 घंटे बाद कितनी गतिविधि बचेगी?
e: After 2 half-lives (6+6=12 hours), the activity reduces to 1/2 of 1/2, which is 1/4 or 25%.

qe: Which unit is used to measure 'Radioactivity' (disintegrations per second)?
qh: 'रेडियोधर्मिता' को मापने के लिए किस इकाई का उपयोग किया जाता है?
e: One Becquerel is defined as one nuclear disintegration per second. The older unit was the curie, and one curie equals 3.7 into ten to the power ten becquerels.

qe: The 'Radium series' ends when it decays into which stable element?
qh: 'रेडियम श्रृंखला' किस स्थिर तत्व में क्षय होने पर समाप्त होती है?
e: The natural radioactive series of radium eventually reaches a stable isotope of lead. The series starts from uranium-238 and passes through radium and radon, and it ends in a stable isotope of lead.

qe: What are 'Alpha particles' composed of?
qh: 'अल्फा कण' (Alpha particles) किससे बने होते हैं?
o: 2 Protons and 2 Neutrons | 2 प्रोटॉन और 2 न्यूट्रॉन
e: Alpha particles are helium nuclei emitted from unstable heavy atoms. They are given out by heavy nuclei such as uranium and radium and carry a double positive charge.

qe: What is the charge of a 'Gamma ray'?
qh: 'गामा किरण' (Gamma ray) का आवेश क्या है?
e: Gamma rays are neutral electromagnetic radiation, not particles. Gamma rays are electromagnetic rays like light with no mass and no charge, and they need thick lead or concrete to be stopped.

qe: Artificial isotopes like 'Technetium-99m' are used in imaging because:
qh: इमेजिंग में 'टेक्नेटियम-99m' जैसे कृत्रिम आइसोटोप का उपयोग किया जाता है क्योंकि:
o: They have a short half-life and emit gamma | छोटी हाफ-लाइफ
e: Short half-life isotopes reduce radiation dose to the patient while providing clear images.

qe: The process where an unstable nucleus loses energy by emitting radiation is:
qh: वह प्रक्रिया जिसमें एक अस्थिर नाभिक विकिरण उत्सर्जित करके ऊर्जा खो देता है:
e: This is the fundamental definition of radioactivity and unstable atoms. The nucleus may give out alpha particles, beta particles or gamma rays, and it turns into a different element.

qe: Which type of decay occurs when a neutron turns into a proton and emits an electron?
qh: जब न्यूट्रॉन प्रोटॉन में बदल जाता है और इलेक्ट्रॉन उत्सर्जित करता है, तो कौन सा क्षय होता है?
e: Beta particles are high-speed electrons or positrons emitted during nuclear decay. In this decay the atomic number rises by one while the mass number remains the same.

qe: The 'Lead container' used for radium storage is an example of:
qh: रेडियम भंडारण के लिए उपयोग किया जाने वाला 'सीसा कंटेनर' किसका उदाहरण है?
e: Lead is a high-density material used to block harmful radioactive emissions. The thick lead wall absorbs the radiation and also keeps the source from being touched or dropped.

qe: Radioactive 'Tracers' in imaging help to study:
qh: इमेजिंग में रेडियोधर्मी 'ट्रेसर' किसके अध्ययन में मदद करते हैं?
o: Organ function and metabolism | अंग कार्य और चयापचय
e: Isotopes in imaging provide functional information rather than just structural details. A small dose of the tracer is given to the patient, and its path in the organ is pictured with a gamma camera.

qe: Why is 'Copper' used in the anode body along with the Tungsten target?
qh: टंगस्टन टारगेट के साथ एनोड बॉडी में 'कॉपर' का उपयोग क्यों किया जाता है?
o: To dissipate heat quickly | गर्मी को जल्दी सोखने के लिए
e: Copper is a great thermal conductor, helping to remove the 99% heat generated during X-ray production.

qe: The 'Line Focus Principle' is used in X-ray tubes to:
qh: एक्स-रे ट्यूब में 'लाइन फोकस सिद्धांत' का उपयोग किया जाता है:
o: Reduce effective focal spot size | प्रभावी फोकल स्पॉट आकार कम करना
e: It allows a large actual focal spot for heat loading while maintaining a small effective focal spot for image sharpness.

qe: What is the relationship between X-ray wavelength and frequency?
qh: एक्स-रे तरंग दैर्ध्य (wavelength) और आवृत्ति (frequency) के बीच क्या संबंध है?
e: Higher frequency means shorter wavelength and higher energy. The two are related by the equation speed equals frequency multiplied by wavelength, and for X-rays the speed is that of light.

qe: Which interaction produces 'Characteristic Radiation' in the X-ray tube?
qh: एक्स-रे ट्यूब में कौन सी परस्पर क्रिया 'विशिष्ट विकिरण' (Characteristic Radiation) उत्पन्न करती है?
o: Inner shell (K-shell) ionization | आंतरिक शेल (K-shell) आयनीकरण
e: Characteristic X-rays are produced when an inner shell electron is ejected and replaced by an outer shell electron.

qe: What is 'Bremsstrahlung' radiation?
qh: 'ब्रेम्सस्ट्रालुंग' (Bremsstrahlung) विकिरण क्या है?
e: It occurs when an electron is slowed down or 'braked' by the nucleus of the target atom. These rays have a range of energies, and they form the general or continuous part of the X-ray spectrum.

qe: How does increasing 'mA' (milliamperage) affect the X-ray beam?
qh: 'mA' बढ़ाने से एक्स-रे बीम पर क्या प्रभाव पड़ता है?
o: Increases quantity of X-rays | एक्स-रे की मात्रा बढ़ाता है
e: mA controls the number of electrons boiled off the filament, thus controlling beam intensity.

qe: The 'Actual Focal Spot' is located on the:
qh: 'एक्चुअल फोकल स्पॉट' कहाँ स्थित होता है?
e: It is the area on the target that is physically struck by the electron stream. Because the target is angled, the area seen from the film side is smaller than the actual focal spot.

qe: Which component of the X-ray tube is negatively charged?
qh: एक्स-रे ट्यूब का कौन सा घटक नकारात्मक रूप से आवेशित होता है?
e: The cathode contains the filament and focusing cup which push electrons toward the anode. The filament becomes hot and gives out electrons, and the focusing cup keeps them together on their way to the target.

qe: The process of removing low-energy X-ray photons is called:
qh: कम ऊर्जा वाले एक्स-रे फोटॉनों को हटाने की प्रक्रिया कहलाती है:
e: Filtration 'hardens' the beam by removing soft X-rays that only add to patient dose. It is done by the glass and oil of the tube itself and by added sheets of aluminium, and it lowers the patient dose.

qe: What percentage of electron energy is converted to X-rays in a standard tube?
qh: एक मानक ट्यूब में इलेक्ट्रॉन ऊर्जा का कितना प्रतिशत एक्स-रे में परिवर्तित होता है?
e: Over 99% of kinetic energy is converted to heat, and less than 1% becomes X-rays. For this reason the tube has a rotating anode and oil cooling, and its heat capacity puts a limit on long runs.

qe: What is 'Half-life' in radioactivity?
qh: रेडियोधर्मिता में 'हाफ-लाइफ' (Half-life) क्या है?
o: Time taken for half of the atoms to decay | आधा क्षय होने में लगा समय
e: Half-life is the time required for the activity of a radioactive source to reduce by half.

qe: Unstable atoms that undergo spontaneous decay are called:
qh: स्वतः क्षय होने वाले अस्थिर परमाणुओं को कहा जाता है:
e: Radioactivity is the property of unstable atomic nuclei. Such atoms are called radioactive, and their nuclei break up at a fixed rate that heat or pressure cannot change.

qe: Which series describes the natural decay of Radium?
qh: कौन सी श्रृंखला रेडियम के प्राकृतिक क्षय का वर्णन करती है?
e: The Radium series tracks the stages of decay from parent to stable lead. The series begins with uranium-238, passes through radium and radon, and ends in lead.

qe: What are 'Isotopes' used for in medical imaging?
qh: मेडिकल इमेजिंग में 'आइसोटोप' (Isotopes) का उपयोग किसके लिए किया जाता है?
o: As radioactive tracers | रेडियोधर्मी ट्रेसर के रूप में
e: Artificial radioactivity allows isotopes to be used as tracers in functional imaging. A very small amount is given, and the organ that takes it up can be pictured; the same property is used to treat some diseases.

qe: The definition of 'Artificial Radioactivity' is:
qh: 'कृत्रिम रेडियोधर्मिता' (Artificial Radioactivity) की परिभाषा है:
o: Radioactivity induced by bombarding stable elements | प्रेरित रेडियोधर्मिता
e: Man-made radioactive elements are produced by bombarding stable nuclei. Such isotopes are made in a reactor or a cyclotron, and examples are cobalt-60 and technetium-99m.

qe: Which type of 'Radioactive radiation' has the highest penetrating power?
qh: किस प्रकार के 'रेडियोधर्मी विकिरण' में सबसे अधिक मर्मज्ञ शक्ति होती है?
e: Gamma rays are high-energy photons with very high penetration. Gamma rays are stopped only by thick lead or concrete, while alpha and beta rays are stopped by paper or a thin metal sheet.

qe: In radiology, 'Radio Dosage' management includes the use of:
qh: रेडियोलॉजी में 'रेडियो डोज' प्रबंधन में किसका उपयोग शामिल है?
o: Filtration and Containers | निस्पंदन और कंटेनर
e: Shielding and filtration are used to protect patients and staff from excess dose. It also includes the ALARA principle, correct kV and mAs, collimation and the use of a fast film-screen or digital system.

qe: What is the primary risk of handling 'Unstable atoms'?
qh: 'अस्थिर परमाणुओं' को संभालने का प्राथमिक जोखिम क्या है?
o: Ionizing radiation exposure | आयनकारी विकिरण जोखिम
e: Unstable atoms emit radiation that can cause biological damage. The radiation can break the DNA, burn the skin in large doses and cause cancer after long exposure.

qe: Which applicator is used for 'Protection' against radioactive losses?
qh: रेडियोधर्मी नुकसान के खिलाफ 'सुरक्षा' (Protection) के लिए किस एप्लिकेटर का उपयोग किया जाता है?
e: Protection involves using containers that block harmful radiation emissions. Tongs are used to handle the source, and the time spent near it is kept as short as possible.

qe: Radioactive series eventually end with the formation of:
qh: रेडियोधर्मी श्रृंखला अंततः किसके निर्माण के साथ समाप्त होती है?
e: Unstable elements decay until they reach a stable, non-radioactive state. The chain finally gives a stable element such as lead, which gives out no more radiation.

qe: Who discovered X-Rays in the year 1895?
qh: 1895 में एक्स-रे की खोज किसने की थी?
o: Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen | विल्हेम कॉनराड रॉन्टगन
e: X-rays were discovered by Roentgen, which is why they are also called Roentgen Rays. He received the first Nobel Prize in Physics for the discovery, and the rays were used in medicine within a year.

qe: Which material is most commonly used as a 'Target material' in an X-ray tube?
qh: एक्स-रे ट्यूब में 'टारगेट सामग्री' के रूप में आमतौर पर किस सामग्री का उपयोग किया जाता है?
e: Tungsten is used because of its high atomic number and high melting point. It has a high atomic number and a melting point of about 3400 degrees Celsius, so it bears the heat of the electron beam.

qe: What determines the 'Quality' or penetrating power of X-rays?
qh: एक्स-रे की 'गुणवत्ता' या मर्मज्ञ शक्ति (penetrating power) क्या निर्धारित करती है?
e: Voltage (kVp) determines the energy and quality of the X-ray beam. A higher kVp gives shorter wavelength and more penetrating rays, while the mA and the time decide the quantity of X-rays.

qe: What are 'Hard X-rays'?
qh: 'कठोर एक्स-रे' (Hard X-rays) क्या हैं?
o: High energy rays with high penetration | उच्च ऊर्जा वाली किरणें
e: Hard X-rays have shorter wavelengths and higher penetrating power. They are produced at a higher kilovoltage and are used for thick or dense parts, while the soft rays are filtered out.

qe: X-rays are a form of which type of radiation?
qh: एक्स-रे किस प्रकार के विकिरण का एक रूप हैं?
e: X-rays travel at the speed of light as electromagnetic waves. They have no mass and no charge, travel in straight lines, and behave as packets of energy called photons.

qe: The interaction of penetrating radiation with 'Matter' involves:
qh: मर्मज्ञ विकिरण की 'पदार्थ' (Matter) के साथ परस्पर क्रिया में शामिल है:
o: Absorption and Scattering | अवशोषण और प्रकीर्णन
e: When X-rays hit matter, they can be absorbed or scattered. In absorption the energy is taken up by the atom, while in scattering the ray changes its direction, the photoelectric and Compton effects being the two main ways.

qe: Which property of X-rays makes them useful for medical imaging?
qh: एक्स-रे का कौन सा गुण उन्हें मेडिकल इमेजिंग के लिए उपयोगी बनाता है?
o: Differential absorption by tissues | ऊतकों द्वारा विभेदक अवशोषण
e: Different body tissues absorb X-rays at different rates, creating an image. Bone absorbs more than soft tissue and air absorbs the least, so the film shows a clear difference between them.

qe: What is the result of using a 'Soft X-ray' beam?
qh: 'नरम एक्स-रे' (Soft X-ray) बीम के उपयोग का परिणाम क्या होता है?
o: Low penetration and higher skin dose | कम मर्मज्ञ शक्ति
e: Soft X-rays have longer wavelengths and are easily absorbed by the skin. The beam does not reach the film properly, so the picture is light and the patient also gets an unwanted dose.

qe: The 'Source' of electrons in a modern X-ray tube is the:
qh: आधुनिक एक्स-रे ट्यूब में इलेक्ट्रॉनों का 'स्रोत' है:
e: Thermionic emission from the filament provides the electrons needed. The filament is heated by a small current, and the electrons given out are pulled to the anode by the high voltage.

qe: Why is vacuum maintained inside the X-ray tube?
qh: एक्स-रे ट्यूब के अंदर वैक्यूम क्यों बनाए रखा जाता है?
o: To prevent electron collision with air molecules | हवा के अणुओं से टकराव रोकने के लिए
e: Vacuum allows electrons to travel from cathode to anode without obstruction. A vacuum also stops the electrons from colliding with air molecules and protects the hot filament from burning out.

qe: Which sense is defined by the term 'Olfaction'?
qh: 'ऑल्फैक्शन' (Olfaction) शब्द किस इंद्रिय को परिभाषित करता है?
o: Sense of smell | गंध की अनुभूति
e: Taste, olfaction, and visceral sensations are key somatic sensations studied. The receptors lie in the upper part of the nasal cavity and send signals to the brain through the olfactory nerve.

qe: The 'Visceral sensations' relate to which part of the body?
qh: 'विसरल सेंसेशन्स' (Visceral sensations) शरीर के किस भाग से संबंधित हैं?
e: Visceral sensations provide information about the status of internal body organs. They arise from the internal organs such as the stomach and the bladder and are carried by the autonomic nerves.

qe: What happens to 'Fluid distribution' during heavy exercise?
qh: भारी व्यायाम के दौरान 'तरल वितरण' (Fluid distribution) का क्या होता है?
o: Changes due to sweating and metabolic needs | पसीने और मेटाबोलिक जरूरतों के कारण बदलाव
e: Body fluid changes and exchange are critical responses to exercise and work. Water and salts are lost in sweat, the blood flow shifts to the muscles and the plasma volume falls, so the fluid must be replaced.

qe: Which system is analyzed for 'Skill, Strength, and Endurance'?
qh: 'कौशल, शक्ति और धीरज' के लिए किस तंत्र का विश्लेषण किया जाता है?
o: Neuromuscular and Respiratory | न्यूरोमस्कुलर और श्वसन
e: Physiological mechanism in movement behavior includes analyzing skill and endurance. It studies how the body responds to work, including muscle action, energy use and recovery.

qe: Efficiency of 'Muscular work' is affected by:
qh: 'मांसपेशियों के कार्य' की दक्षता किससे प्रभावित होती है?
o: Environmental factors and nutrition | पर्यावरणीय कारक और पोषण
e: Metabolic and environmental aspects like heat affect muscular efficiency. The efficiency falls in extreme heat or cold, in high humidity and in poor nutrition, and it improves with training.

qe: The study of 'Vision' includes the physiological function of:
qh: 'दृष्टि' (Vision) के अध्ययन में किसका शारीरिक कार्य शामिल है?
o: Retina and Optic nerve | रेटिना और ऑप्टिक तंत्रिका
e: Neuro-physiology covers the mechanics of vision and sensory end organs. It covers the eye, the retina, the optic nerve and the visual cortex, and the way images are formed and perceived.

qe: What is the result of 'Fatigue' in the body?
qh: शरीर में 'थकान' (Fatigue) का क्या परिणाम होता है?
o: Temporary decrease in work capacity | कार्य क्षमता में अस्थायी कमी
e: Fatigue and training involve endurance fatigue and recovery processes. It lowers the power of the muscle, slows the reaction time and spoils the quality of work, and rest restores it.

qe: Medical aspects of exercise take into account:
qh: व्यायाम के चिकित्सा पहलुओं में किसे ध्यान में रखा जाता है?
o: Age, Sex, and Race | आयु, लिंग और जाति
e: Fitness and health stress are analyzed based on individual body types and age. Age, sex, body type and the presence of disease decide how much and what kind of exercise is safe for a person.

qe: Which part of the nervous system is responsible for the 'Reflex physiology' of organs?
qh: अंगों की 'रिफ्लेक्स फिजियोलॉजी' के लिए तंत्रिका तंत्र का कौन सा भाग जिम्मेदार है?
o: Autonomic Nervous System | ऑटोनोमिक नर्वस सिस्टम
e: The autonomic system manages reflex physiology of visceral organs. It works without our will and controls the heart, the gut, the glands and the blood vessels.

qe: The term 'Endurance fatigue' refers to exhaustion after:
qh: 'एंड्योरेंस थकान' (Endurance fatigue) का तात्पर्य किसके बाद होने वाली थकावट से है?
o: Prolonged physical activity | लंबे समय तक शारीरिक गतिविधि
e: Endurance training aims to delay this specific type of fatigue. It appears in long and tiring work, and training lengthens the time for which a person can keep up the effort.

qe: The 'Electro-physiological' activity of the heart begins at which natural pacemaker?
qh: हृदय की 'इलेक्ट्रो-फिजियोलॉजिकल' गतिविधि किस प्राकृतिक पेसमेकर से शुरू होती है?
o: SA Node (Sinoatrial node) | एसए नोड (SA Node)
e: The SA node initiates the electrical impulse, studied under the electro-physiological activity of the heart.

qe: What does the 'P-wave' represent in a normal ECG?
qh: एक सामान्य ECG में 'P-वेव' क्या दर्शाती है?
e: The P-wave indicates the electrical activity and mechanical contraction of the atria. It is a small upward wave before the QRS complex, and it is followed by the contraction of the atria.

qe: Which part of the brain is responsible for 'Cortical Control' of movements?
qh: गतिविधियों के 'कोर्टिकल कंट्रोल' के लिए मस्तिष्क का कौन सा भाग जिम्मेदार है?
e: Cortical control refers to the voluntary management of motor functions by the brain's cortex.

qe: The 'Synapse' is a specialized property used for:
qh: 'सिंकैप्स' (Synapse) एक विशिष्ट गुण है जिसका उपयोग किया जाता है:
o: Communication between two neurons | दो न्यूरॉन्स के बीच संचार
e: Synapses are key sites for nerve impulse transmission and potential gradients. The impulse crosses the small gap with the help of a chemical transmitter, and the signal can be modified at this point.

qe: What is 'Supraspinal Control' in neuro-physiology?
qh: न्यूरो-फिजियोलॉजी में 'सुप्रास्पाइनल कंट्रोल' (Supraspinal Control) क्या है?
o: Control of reflexes by higher brain centers | उच्च मस्तिष्क केंद्रों द्वारा नियंत्रण
e: Supraspinal control involves higher brain regions regulating spinal reflex activity. The cortex and the brain stem send impulses down to control and adjust the reflexes of the spinal cord.

qe: The 'Coronary circulation' primarily supplies blood to:
qh: 'कोरोनरी सर्कुलेशन' मुख्य रूप से किसे रक्त की आपूर्ति करता है?
e: Coronary circulation ensures the heart muscle receives enough oxygen and nutrients. The right and left coronary arteries arise from the aorta, and their blockage causes a heart attack.

qe: Which ions are primarily responsible for the 'Action Potential' in nerves?
qh: तंत्रिकाओं में 'एक्शन पोटेंशियल' के लिए मुख्य रूप से कौन से आयन जिम्मेदार हैं?
o: Sodium and Potassium | सोडियम और पोटेशियम
e: Ionic and potential gradients across the cell membrane create the action potential. Sodium ions rush into the cell and potassium ions move out, which changes the charge across the membrane.

qe: The 'Basal ganglia' work with the cerebellum to control:
qh: 'बेसल गैन्ग्लिया' सेरेबेलम के साथ मिलकर किसे नियंत्रित करते हैं?
o: Smoothness and planning of movement | आंदोलन की सुगमता
e: Basal ganglia are vital for motor mechanism and biophysics of movement. They start and smooth the movements, and damage here causes stiffness, tremor and slowness of movement.

qe: Which property allows a nerve fiber to respond to a stimulus?
qh: कौन सा गुण तंत्रिका फाइबर को उत्तेजना पर प्रतिक्रिया करने की अनुमति देता है?
e: Excitability is a special property of nerve trunks and tracts. A stimulus changes the permeability of the membrane and starts the action potential, which then travels along the fibre.

qe: Mechanical activity of the heart includes which phase?
qh: हृदय की यांत्रिक गतिविधि में कौन सा चरण शामिल है?
o: Systole and Diastole | सिस्टोल और डायस्टोल
e: Systole (contraction) and Diastole (relaxation) are the mechanical actions of the heart. During systole the blood is pumped out, and during diastole the chambers fill again.

qe: In the 'Physiology of Exercise', what is meant by 'Endurance'?
qh: 'व्यायाम की फिजियोलॉजी' में 'धीरज' (Endurance) का क्या अर्थ है?
o: Ability to sustain activity over time | गतिविधि को लंबे समय तक जारी रखना
e: Endurance fatigue and recovery training are key aspects of exercise physiology. It is the ability to continue an activity for a long time, and it depends on the heart, the lungs, the muscles and the energy stores.

qe: How does 'Training' affect fatigue during work?
qh: 'प्रशिक्षण' (Training) कार्य के दौरान थकान को कैसे प्रभावित करता है?
o: Delays fatigue and improves recovery | थकान में देरी और रिकवरी में सुधार
e: Training improves the body's efficiency and ability to recover from strenuous work. Training improves the blood supply to the muscles, increases the energy stores and makes the work feel easier.

qe: Which metabolic aspect is essential for providing 'Energy' for muscular work?
qh: मांसपेशियों के कार्य के लिए 'ऊर्जा' प्रदान करने के लिए कौन सा मेटाबोलिक पहलू आवश्यक है?
o: Metabolism and nutrition | चयापचय और पोषण
e: Energy requirement and nutritional aspects dictate the efficiency of muscular work. The energy comes from the breakdown of glucose and fat with oxygen, and a small part is used without oxygen.

qe: The 'Circulatory response' to exercise involves an increase in:
qh: व्यायाम के प्रति 'परिसंचरण प्रतिक्रिया' में किसकी वृद्धि शामिल है?
o: Heart rate and blood flow | हृदय गति और रक्त प्रवाह
e: Exercise triggers respiratory and circulatory responses to transport more oxygen. The heart rate, stroke volume and blood pressure rise, and the blood is diverted from the gut to the working muscles.

qe: What happens to 'Body Temperature' during heavy muscular work?
qh: भारी मांसपेशियों के काम के दौरान 'शरीर के तापमान' का क्या होता है?
e: Muscular work generates heat as a metabolic byproduct, raising body temperature. Heat is produced faster than it is lost, so sweating starts and the skin vessels open to cool the body.

qe: The 'Neuromuscular activity' analysis includes the study of:
qh: 'न्यूरोमस्कुलर गतिविधि' के विश्लेषण में किसका अध्ययन शामिल है?
o: Human movement and skill behavior | मानव आंदोलन और कौशल व्यवहार
e: Exercise physiology studies the physiological mechanism in movement behavior. It covers the motor unit, the nerve impulse, the muscle action and the coordination of the movement.

qe: Which factor is a 'medical aspect' of exercise related to stress?
qh: व्यायाम का कौन सा कारक तनाव से संबंधित 'चिकित्सा पहलू' (Medical aspect) है?
o: Fitness and health stress | फिटनेस और स्वास्थ्य तनाव
e: Stress, medical aspects, and fitness are studied across different ages and sexes. Disease, injury and stress change the response to exercise, so exercise is prescribed according to the person's health.

qe: A 'Reflex arc' is the basic unit of:
qh: 'रिफ्लेक्स आर्क' (Reflex arc) किसकी मूल इकाई है?
e: Reflex physiology governs the body's automatic responses to stimuli. It consists of a receptor, a sensory nerve, a centre in the spinal cord, a motor nerve and the effector organ.

qe: What is the primary role of 'Vision' and 'Auditory system' in movement?
qh: आंदोलन में 'दृष्टि' और 'श्रवण प्रणाली' की प्राथमिक भूमिका क्या है?
o: Providing sensory feedback for skill | कौशल के लिए संवेदी प्रतिक्रिया
e: Sensory inputs are crucial for skilled human movement and analysis. The eyes and ears give information about the position, balance and surroundings, which the brain uses to plan the movement.

qe: Body fluid changes during exercise are often regulated by:
qh: व्यायाम के दौरान शरीर के तरल पदार्थ में परिवर्तन अक्सर किसके द्वारा नियंत्रित होते हैं?
o: Sweating and Renal regulation | पसीना और गुर्दे का विनियमन
e: Fluid distribution and exchange are vital during physical environmental stress. The kidneys reduce the urine output, and the hormones aldosterone and ADH hold back water and salts.

qe: Which condition is defined as a deficiency in the amount of oxygen reaching the tissues?
qh: ऊतकों तक पहुँचने वाली ऑक्सीजन की मात्रा में कमी को क्या कहा जाता है?
e: Hypoxia is a critical state studied in respiratory physiology where tissues lack oxygen. It may be due to lung disease, high altitude or poor blood supply, and it causes breathlessness and bluish lips.

qe: What is the clinical term for 'Difficulty in breathing'?
qh: 'सांस लेने में कठिनाई' के लिए नैदानिक शब्द क्या है?
e: Dyspnoea refers to the sensation of difficult or labored breathing. It may be caused by disease of the lungs or heart, anaemia or anxiety, and it is graded by the effort that provokes it.

qe: The process of 'Resuscitation' is primarily used to treat:
qh: 'रिससिटेशन' (Resuscitation) की प्रक्रिया मुख्य रूप से किसके इलाज के लिए उपयोग की जाती है?
o: Respiratory or Cardiac failure | श्वसन या हृदय की विफलता
e: Resuscitation includes techniques like CPR to restore breathing and circulation. It is used in cardiac arrest, drowning and electric shock, where breathing and circulation have stopped.

qe: Which endocrine gland regulates the 'Basal Metabolic Rate' (BMR)?
qh: कौन सी अंतःस्रावी ग्रंथि 'बेसल मेटाबोलिक रेट' (BMR) को नियंत्रित करती है?
e: The thyroid gland secretes hormones that manage metabolism and energy. Thyroxine raises the rate of oxygen use by the cells, so an overactive gland causes weight loss and a slow gland causes weight gain.

qe: The 'Adrenal glands' are located on top of which organ?
qh: 'एड्रिनल ग्रंथियां' किस अंग के ऊपर स्थित होती हैं?
e: Adrenal glands produce hormones like adrenaline and are situated above the kidneys. The outer cortex makes cortisol and aldosterone, and the inner medulla makes adrenaline.

qe: Which part of the brain controls the 'Autonomic Nervous System'?
qh: मस्तिष्क का कौन सा भाग 'ऑटोनोमिक नर्वस सिस्टम' को नियंत्रित करता है?
e: The hypothalamus serves as the primary control center for the autonomic system. It controls the sympathetic and parasympathetic outflow and keeps the internal environment steady.

qe: The primary function of the 'Gonads' (Testes/Ovaries) is:
qh: 'गोनाड्स' (वृषण/अंडाशय) का प्राथमिक कार्य क्या है?
o: Reproduction and Sex hormone production | प्रजनन और हार्मोन उत्पादन
e: Gonads are part of the endocrine system responsible for reproductive functions. The testes produce sperm and testosterone, and the ovaries produce eggs, oestrogen and progesterone.

qe: What does 'Renal filtration' produce as a waste product?
qh: 'रीनल फिल्ट्रेशन' अपशिष्ट उत्पाद के रूप में क्या उत्पन्न करता है?
e: Renal function involves filtering the blood to produce urine for excretion. About 180 litres of filtrate are formed daily, most of it is reabsorbed, and about 1.5 litres of urine are left.

qe: Which hormone is produced by the 'Pancreas' to lower blood sugar?
qh: रक्त शर्करा को कम करने के लिए 'अग्न्याशय' द्वारा कौन सा हार्मोन बनाया जाता है?
e: Insulin is critical for regulating glucose levels in the blood system. It is made by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans and moves glucose from the blood into the cells.

qe: The exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the alveoli is called:
qh: एल्वियोली में ऑक्सीजन और कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड के विनिमय को कहा जाता है?
o: External/Pulmonary gas exchange | बाहरी/पल्मोनरी गैस विनिमय
e: Pulmonary gas exchange occurs between the air in the lungs and the blood. Oxygen passes from the air into the blood and carbon dioxide passes from the blood into the air, both by simple diffusion.

qe: The 'Action Potential' in a nerve cell is an example of:
qh: तंत्रिका कोशिका में 'एक्शन पोटेंशियल' किसका एक उदाहरण है?
o: Electrical signal transmission | विद्युत संकेत संचरण
e: Action potential is a key part of neuro-physiology and ionic transport. It is a wave of electrical change that travels along the nerve or muscle membrane without losing its strength.

qe: What is the basic functional unit of muscle contraction?
qh: मांसपेशियों के संकुचन की मूल कार्यात्मक इकाई क्या है?
e: Motor units are essential for understanding muscle mechanism and biophysics. It is one motor neuron together with all the muscle fibres that it supplies, and the number of units decides the precision of movement.

qe: The state of reduced capacity for work due to previous activity is called:
qh: पिछली गतिविधि के कारण काम करने की कम क्षमता वाली स्थिति कहलाती है:
e: Fatigue results from metabolic and environmental aspects of exercise and work. It follows prolonged work, and it is due to the use of the energy stores, the collection of waste products and the strain on the nervous system.

qe: Which system is responsible for 'Reflex physiology'?
qh: 'रिफ्लेक्स फिजियोलॉजी' के लिए कौन सा तंत्र जिम्मेदार है?
e: Reflex physiology involve synapses and supraspinal control within the nervous system. It includes the reflex arc, the spinal reflexes and the control exercised by the higher centres.

qe: The 'Auditory system' is responsible for which sense?
qh: 'ऑडिटरी सिस्टम' (Auditory system) किस इंद्रिय के लिए जिम्मेदार है?
e: The auditory system and vision are key somatic sensations studied in physiology. The sound waves are collected by the ear, turned into nerve impulses in the cochlea and carried to the brain.

qe: During exercise, 'Pulmonary ventilation' increases to:
qh: व्यायाम के दौरान, 'पल्मोनरी वेंटिलेशन' क्यों बढ़ जाता है?
o: Increase gas exchange | गैस विनिमय बढ़ाने के लिए
e: Respiratory response to work involves increased gas transport and ventilation. The depth and the rate of breathing both increase, so more oxygen is taken in and the extra carbon dioxide is thrown out.

qe: Which gland regulates calcium levels in the body?
qh: शरीर में कैल्शियम के स्तर को कौन सी ग्रंथि नियंत्रित करती है?
e: Parathyroid glands are part of the endocrine system alongside the thyroid. The parathyroid hormone raises the blood calcium by acting on the bones, the gut and the kidneys, and it is opposed by thyrocalcitonin.

qe: The study of 'Skill, Strength, and Endurance' falls under:
qh: 'कौशल, शक्ति और धीरज' का अध्ययन किसके अंतर्गत आता है?
o: Physiology of Exercise | व्यायाम की फिजियोलॉजी
e: Exercise physiology analyzes movement behavior and human performance. It explains how the muscles, heart, lungs and nerves work together during work and how training changes them.

qe: Which structure facilitates communication between two neurons?
qh: दो न्यूरॉन्स के बीच संचार की सुविधा कौन सी संरचना प्रदान करती है?
e: Synapses are the points of connection for nerve impulse transmission. The impulse crosses the small gap with the help of a chemical transmitter released from the end of the nerve.

qe: Environmental aspects of work include the regulation of:
qh: कार्य के पर्यावरणीय पहलुओं में किसका नियमन शामिल है?
o: Heat and body temperature | गर्मी और शरीर का तापमान
e: Metabolic and environmental factors affect the efficiency of muscular work. The temperature and humidity of the workplace, the noise and the working hours all affect efficiency and health.

qe: What is the primary function of the 'Cell Membrane'?
qh: 'कोशिका झिल्ली' (Cell Membrane) का प्राथमिक कार्य क्या है?
o: Selective transport of substances | पदार्थों का चयनात्मक परिवहन
e: The cell membrane regulates the entry and exit of ions and potential gradients. It is a thin semi-permeable layer that keeps the cell contents in place and also carries the receptors and pumps.

qe: Which component of blood is responsible for 'Coagulation'?
qh: रक्त का कौन सा घटक 'कोगुलेशन' (थक्का जमने) के लिए जिम्मेदार है?
o: Platelets and Fibrinogen | प्लेटलेट्स और फाइब्रिनोजेन
e: Coagulation is a vital part of the blood system to prevent excessive bleeding. Platelets and the clotting factors of the plasma act together to form a clot and stop the bleeding.

qe: The 'Electro-physiological activity' of the heart is recorded using which test?
qh: हृदय की 'इलेक्ट्रो-फिजियोलॉजिकल' गतिविधि को किस टेस्ट का उपयोग करके रिकॉर्ड किया जाता है?
e: Physiology covers both the mechanical and electro-physiological activity of the heart. The ECG records the electrical changes of the heart on paper and helps to detect rhythm and conduction defects.

qe: What is the primary function of 'Hemoglobin'?
qh: 'हीमोग्लोबिन' का प्राथमिक कार्य क्या है?
e: Hemoglobin within erythrocytes carries respiratory gases throughout the body. It takes up oxygen in the lungs and gives it to the tissues, and it also carries a part of the carbon dioxide.

qe: Which blood cells are primarily involved in the 'Immune response'?
qh: कौन सी रक्त कोशिकाएं मुख्य रूप से 'प्रतिरक्षा प्रतिक्रिया' में शामिल होती हैं?
e: Lymphocytes are key cells in the body's cell renewal and immune system. They make antibodies and also attack the infected cells directly, so they form the body's defence against microbes.

qe: The regulation of 'Hydrogen ion concentration' in body fluids relates to:
qh: शरीर के तरल पदार्थों में 'हाइड्रोजन आयन सांद्रता' का विनियमन किससे संबंधित है?
e: Maintaining the concentration of hydrogen ions is essential for body fluid distribution. The pH of the blood is kept between 7.35 and 7.45 by the lungs, the kidneys and the buffer systems.

qe: Which gland is known as the 'Master Gland' of the endocrine system?
qh: अंतःस्रावी तंत्र की किस ग्रंथि को 'मास्टर ग्रंथि' के रूप में जाना जाता है?
e: The pituitary gland regulates other endocrine glands like the thyroid and adrenals. It makes hormones that control the thyroid, the adrenals, the gonads and growth, and it lies at the base of the brain.

qe: The 'Mechanical activity' of the heart refers to:
qh: हृदय की 'यांत्रिक गतिविधि' (Mechanical activity) का तात्पर्य है:
o: Contraction and Pumping | संकुचन और पंपिंग
e: Physiology studies the mechanical pumping action and coronary circulation of the heart. This includes the filling and emptying of the chambers and the pumping of blood into the aorta and the pulmonary artery.

qe: Which process describes the 'exchange of gases' in the lungs?
qh: फेफड़ों में 'गैसों के विनिमय' का वर्णन कौन सी प्रक्रिया करती है?
o: Pulmonary gas exchange | पल्मोनरी गैस विनिमय
e: Pulmonary gas exchange involves the transport of respiratory gases like oxygen and CO2. It takes place in the alveoli by diffusion, and the blood carries the gases to and from the tissues.

qe: Renal function primarily involves the filtration of:
qh: 'रीनल फंक्शन' (Renal function) में मुख्य रूप से किसका निस्पंदन शामिल है?
o: Blood to form urine | मूत्र बनाने के लिए रक्त
e: The kidneys filter blood to regulate fluid distribution and exchange. The blood is filtered in the glomerulus, the useful substances are taken back and the waste forms urine.

qe: The study of 'Fascias and muscles of head, neck & face' is part of:
qh: 'सिर, गर्दन और चेहरे की मांसपेशियों' का अध्ययन किसका हिस्सा है?
e: This part of anatomy covers the muscles that move the jaw and the face, along with the fascia that holds them in place.

qe: Which type of joints allow for the greatest range of movement?
qh: किस प्रकार के जोड़ सबसे अधिक गति की अनुमति देते हैं?
e: Movements of joints are classified based on the degree of freedom they offer. These are freely movable joints, and their shape allows movement in many directions, as at the shoulder and the hip.

qe: Fascias and muscles of the 'Upper Limb' are essential for:
qh: 'ऊपरी अंग' की मांसपेशियां किसके लिए आवश्यक हैं?
o: Arm and hand movements | हाथ की गति
e: Muscles of the upper limb facilitate reaching, lifting, and fine motor skills. They also help in grasping, writing and throwing, and their fascia keeps the muscles and vessels in place.

qe: Which factor 'limits' the movement of a joint?
qh: कौन सा कारक जोड़ की गति को 'सीमित' करता है?
o: Bone shape and ligaments | हड्डियों का आकार और स्नायुबंधन
e: Anatomy studies the factors permitting and limiting movements in joints. The shape of the bones, the tightness of the ligaments and the tone of the muscles limit the movement.

qe: The joints of the 'Trunks' primarily involve the:
qh: 'धड़' (Trunks) के जोड़ों में मुख्य रूप से शामिल हैं:
e: Joints of the trunk include the intervertebral joints of the spine. These joints allow bending forward and backward, side bending and rotation of the spine.

qe: Which part of the brain coordinates complex muscular movements?
qh: मस्तिष्क का कौन सा भाग जटिल मांसपेशियों की गतिविधियों का समन्वय करता है?
e: The cerebellum is the center for motor coordination and balance. It keeps the movements smooth, maintains balance and corrects the errors noticed during an action.

qe: Surface Anatomy is used to study:
qh: सर्फेस एनाटॉमी का उपयोग किसके अध्ययन के लिए किया जाता है?
o: Surface landmarks on the human body | शरीर के सतही स्थलचिह्न
e: Surface anatomy focuses on identifying internal structures via external body landmarks. It helps a doctor to locate the pulsations, the bony points and the organs before examining or operating on a patient.

qe: Muscles of the 'Lower Limb' are primarily responsible for:
qh: 'निचले अंग' की मांसपेशियां मुख्य रूप से किसके लिए जिम्मेदार हैं?
o: Walking and Posture | चलना और मुद्रा
e: The lower limb musculature supports the body's weight and enables locomotion. They also help in standing, walking, running and climbing, and their fascia forms a strong covering around them.

qe: Which structure facilitates 'Neuromuscular Function'?
qh: 'न्यूरोमस्कुलर फंक्शन' (Neuromuscular Function) को कौन सी संरचना सुगम बनाती है?
e: Anatomy covers the integration of nerves and muscles for movement. The motor nerve ending and the muscle fibre form the junction where a nerve signal starts the muscle contraction.

qe: The 'Basal Ganglia' are involved in which function?
qh: 'बेसल गैन्ग्लिया' (Basal Ganglia) किस कार्य में शामिल हैं?
o: Motor control and Skill learning | मोटर नियंत्रण
e: Basal ganglia work with the cerebellum for smooth motor activities. They help in starting and regulating the voluntary movements, and their damage causes rigidity and tremor.

qe: The 'Superior Colliculi' in the brain are primarily involved in:
qh: मस्तिष्क में 'सुपीरियर कोलीकुली' (Superior Colliculi) मुख्य रूप से किसमें शामिल हैं?
o: Visual reflexes and tracking | विजुअल रिफ्लेक्सिस
e: Superior colliculi are part of the midbrain responsible for visual processing and eye movements.

qe: Which part of the brain acts as the primary relay station for almost all sensory information?
qh: मस्तिष्क का कौन सा भाग लगभग सभी संवेदी सूचनाओं के लिए प्राथमिक रिले स्टेशन है?
e: The thalamus processes and relays sensory impulses to the cerebral cortex. All the sensory impulses except smell pass through it before reaching the cerebral cortex.

qe: The 'Inferior Colliculi' are centers for which type of reflexes?
qh: 'इन्फीरियर कोलीकुली' (Inferior Colliculi) किस प्रकार के रिफ्लेक्सिस के केंद्र हैं?
e: Inferior colliculi are part of the midbrain involved in the auditory pathway. They form a part of the auditory pathway and help in turning the head and eyes towards a sudden sound.

qe: Which structure connects the spinal cord to the higher brain centers?
qh: कौन सी संरचना रीढ़ की हड्डी को मस्तिष्क के उच्च केंद्रों से जोड़ती है?
e: The brainstem includes the medulla, pons, and midbrain, connecting the spinal cord to the brain.

qe: The 'Hypothalamus' is located in which region of the brain?
qh: 'हाइपोथैलेमस' मस्तिष्क के किस क्षेत्र में स्थित है?
e: The hypothalamus is a key part of the diencephalon regulating homeostasis. It lies below the thalamus and controls the autonomic system, temperature, hunger, thirst and the release of hormones.

qe: Which area is responsible for the 'Auditory radiation'?
qh: 'ऑडिटरी रेडिएशन' (Auditory radiation) के लिए कौन सा क्षेत्र जिम्मेदार है?
o: Temporal lobe / Auditory pathway | ऑडिटरी पाथवे
e: Auditory radiation carries sound information from the thalamus to the auditory cortex. It carries the sound impulses from the thalamus to the auditory area of the temporal lobe.

qe: The 'Meninges' consist of how many protective layers?
qh: 'मेनिन्जेस' में कितनी सुरक्षात्मक परतें होती हैं?
e: The meninges include the Dura mater, Arachnoid mater, and Pia mater. They are the dura mater, the arachnoid mater and the pia mater, and the cerebro-spinal fluid circulates between them.

qe: Which structure is involved in 'Intracortical integration'?
qh: 'इंट्राकोर्टिकल इंटीग्रेशन' में कौन सी संरचना शामिल है?
o: Nerve fibers within the cortex | सेरेब्रल कॉर्टेक्स
e: Intracortical integration refers to the processing of information within the layers of the cerebral cortex.

qe: The 'Rhinencephalon' is primarily related to which sense?
qh: 'राइनेंसेफलॉन' (Rhinencephalon) मुख्य रूप से किस इंद्रिय से संबंधित है?
e: The rhinencephalon is the part of the brain involved with the sense of smell. It lies in the temporal lobe and is connected with the sense of smell and with memories linked to it.

qe: Which system manages involuntary motor functions and muscle tone?
qh: कौन सा तंत्र अनैच्छिक मोटर कार्यों और मांसपेशियों के टोन को प्रबंधित करता है?
e: The extra-pyramidal system regulates posture and involuntary muscle movements. It works along with the pyramidal system and the cerebellum to keep the tone, posture and involuntary movements normal.

qe: Which structure provides the 'Blood Supply' to the brain?
qh: मस्तिष्क को 'रक्त आपूर्ति' कौन सी संरचना प्रदान करती है?
o: Circle of Willis / Cerebral arteries | सेरेब्रल धमनियां
e: The brain receives blood primarily through the internal carotid and vertebral arteries. These arteries join at the base of the brain in a circle, and their blockage causes a stroke.

qe: The 'Spinal Cord' is divided into various:
qh: 'रीढ़ की हड्डी' को विभिन्न भागों में विभाजित किया गया है:
o: Segments and Areas | खंड (Segments) और क्षेत्र
e: The spinal cord consists of segments that correspond to pairs of spinal nerves. There are 31 pairs of spinal nerves, one pair for each segment of the cord.

qe: Which part of the brain is responsible for 'Visual Radiation'?
qh: मस्तिष्क का कौन सा भाग 'विजुअल रेडिएशन' के लिए जिम्मेदार है?
o: Diencephalon (pathway to visual cortex) | विजुअल रेडिएशन
e: Visual radiation transmits information from the thalamus to the visual cortex. It carries the visual impulses from the thalamus to the visual cortex in the occipital lobe.

qe: The 'Cerebellum' is primarily involved in:
qh: 'सेरेबेलम' मुख्य रूप से किसमें शामिल है?
o: Motor coordination and Balance | मोटर समन्वय और संतुलन
e: The cerebellum coordinates voluntary movements and posture. It maintains balance, posture and the smoothness of movement, and its damage causes an unsteady gait.

qe: Which ventricles are located within the cerebral hemispheres?
qh: सेरेब्रल हेमिस्फीयर के भीतर कौन से वेंट्रिकल्स स्थित होते हैं?
e: There are two lateral ventricles, one in each hemisphere of the cerebrum. They are two in number, one in each hemisphere, and they contain cerebro-spinal fluid.

qe: The 'Extra-pyramidal system' is involved in:
qh: 'एक्स्ट्रा-पिरामिडल सिस्टम' किसमें शामिल है?
o: Involuntary and smooth motor control | अनैच्छिक मोटर नियंत्रण
e: This system helps regulate muscle tone and posture alongside the pyramidal system. It helps in posture and in the movements that go on without conscious effort, such as swinging the arms while walking.

qe: Fascias and muscles of the 'Trunk' include those of the:
qh: 'धड़' (Trunk) के प्रावरणी और मांसपेशियों में शामिल हैं:
o: Abdomen and Back | पेट और पीठ
e: Trunk muscles support the vertebral column and abdominal wall. They include the muscles of the back, the abdominal wall and the diaphragm, and they keep the body upright.

qe: Which part of the brain contains the 'Thalamus and Hypothalamus'?
qh: मस्तिष्क के किस भाग में 'थैलेमस और हाइपोथैलेमस' होते हैं?
e: The diencephalon is a central region of the brain housing these key structures. It lies deep in the cerebrum and contains the thalamus, the hypothalamus and the pineal gland.

qe: The 'Internal Capsule' is a major pathway for:
qh: 'इंटरनल कैप्सूल' किसके लिए एक प्रमुख मार्ग है?
e: It contains important ascending and descending tracts to and from the cortex. The ascending sensory and descending motor tracts pass through it, so a small lesion here causes a large paralysis.

qe: The study of 'Joints of the Upper Limb' includes:
qh: 'ऊपरी अंग के जोड़ों' के अध्ययन में शामिल हैं:
o: Shoulder, Elbow, and Wrist | कंधा, कोहनी और कलाई
e: These joints allow for the wide range of motion in the arm. They include the shoulder, elbow, wrist and small joints of the hand, and their range of movement is very wide.

qe: The microscopic study of tissues, such as epithelium and connective tissue, is called:
qh: उपकला और संयोजी ऊतक जैसे ऊतकों के सूक्ष्म अध्ययन को कहा जाता है:
e: Histology is the branch of anatomy that deals with the microscopic structure of tissues. The tissues are cut into very thin sections, stained and then seen under the microscope.

qe: Which structure prevents food from entering the trachea during swallowing?
qh: निगलते समय कौन सी संरचना भोजन को श्वासनली में जाने से रोकती है?
e: The epiglottis acts as a lid to the larynx, ensuring food goes into the esophagus. It closes the opening of the larynx during swallowing, and its failure allows food to enter the airway.

qe: The 'Blood Vascular System' includes which of the following components?
qh: 'रक्त संवहनी तंत्र' में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा घटक शामिल है?
o: Arteries, Capillaries, and Veins | धमनियां, केशिकाएं और नसें
e: The vascular system consists of the heart and the vessels that circulate blood. It includes the heart, the arteries, the veins and the capillaries, and it carries oxygen, food and waste products.

qe: Which part of the digestive system is responsible for the microscopic and gross study of food absorption?
qh: पाचन तंत्र का कौन सा भाग भोजन के अवशोषण के सूक्ष्म और स्थूल अध्ययन के लिए जिम्मेदार है?
e: The digestive system includes organs from the mouth to the anus for processing nutrients. Its parts are the mouth, food pipe, stomach, small and large intestine, liver and pancreas, each with its own function.

qe: The primary organ of the 'Lymphatic System' that filters lymph is:
qh: 'लसीका तंत्र' का प्राथमिक अंग जो लसीका को फिल्टर करता है, वह है:
e: Lymphatic vessels and nodes work together to maintain fluid balance and immunity. The spleen filters the blood and the lymph, and it also stores lymphocytes and destroys old red cells.

qe: Which of the following is a major branch of the 'Trachea' entering the lungs?
qh: फेफड़ों में प्रवेश करने वाली 'श्वासनली' की एक प्रमुख शाखा निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी है?
e: The trachea divides into right and left primary bronchi that lead to each lung. The right bronchus is wider and straighter, so an inhaled object usually goes into the right lung.

qe: The study of the development of a 'Fertilized Ovum' is called:
qh: 'निषेचित अंडे' के विकास के अध्ययन को कहा जाता है:
e: Embryology covers fertilization, differentiation, and system development. It covers the formation of the embryo and foetus, the development of the organs and the stages of growth.

qe: Which system is responsible for the excretion of urine from the body?
qh: शरीर से मूत्र के उत्सर्जन के लिए कौन सा तंत्र जिम्मेदार है?
e: The urinary system, part of the urogenital system, manages waste removal. It includes the kidneys, the ureters, the bladder and the urethra, and it removes waste and keeps the water balance.

qe: Bones provide which of the following functions in 'Osteology'?
qh: 'ऑस्टियोलॉजी' में हड्डियाँ निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कार्य प्रदान करती हैं?
o: Formation, Function, and Growth | निर्माण, कार्य और विकास
e: Osteology focuses on the structural and functional aspects of bones. Bones support the body, protect the organs and act as a store of calcium, and the marrow also forms blood cells.

qe: Which tissue type includes 'Cartilage, Bone, and Lymph'?
qh: किस ऊतक प्रकार में 'कार्टिलेज, हड्डी और लसीका' शामिल हैं?
e: These are specialized forms of connective tissue that support the body. They bind, support and protect the other tissues, and they have plenty of intercellular material.

qe: The largest part of the human brain is:
qh: मानव मस्तिष्क का सबसे बड़ा भाग है:
e: The cerebral hemispheres control higher functions like thought and action. It is divided by a deep groove into two hemispheres, and it is the seat of memory and intelligence.

qe: Which part of the brain acts as a relay station for sensory information?
